analysis.title: US Autos & Industrial Tech: 5 days in 5 minutes
key_insights: Busy earnings week for GS auto and industrial tech coverage: VRT, TEL, ST, FLEX, APH, F, BWA, AUR, MBLY, BDC, RIVN, MGA and LEA reported. Common themes were strong datacenter demand, continued industrial end-market recovery, volatile supply chain and input costs pressuring auto profits, and muted global auto unit volumes with weakness in China.
Datacenter demand is very strong for GS Industrial Tech names (APH, VRT, FLEX). Vertiv orders were up more than 100% yoy.

Hyperscaler capex: Google and Amazon maintained 2026 capex guidance, Microsoft modestly lowered its guide on timing, and Meta raised the low end of its range. Reported hyperscalers generally expect capex to rise in 2027.
Datacenter-tied revenue in the quarter was mixed versus investor/consensus expectations at Google, Amazon and Microsoft, though management teams said demand is outpacing supply.
Auto input costs: Ford expects a roughly $2 bn yoy headwind from commodities and logistics in 2027, similar to GM's 3Q call comments. Ford expects roughly flat EBIT yoy in 2027.

US and Canada are reportedly working on a deal to ease Section 232 steel and auto tariffs. A 8/24 post from President Trump said tariffs on Canadian autos and parts could rise to 50% from 25% starting January 2027.
Visteon's CFO Jerome Rouquet leaves effective November 30. Chief Accounting Officer Colleen Myers is interim CFO and a search is under way.
Ford is targeting 5 mn global annual vehicle sales by 2032, versus about 4 mn in 2025 per S&P Global Mobility.
GM plans to invest over $2 bn in its Lansing plants, including the previously announced $1.25 bn for Lansing Grand River Assembly and preparation of Delta Township for future hybrid production.
Audi plans to invest about $4 bn in its first US production site in Georgia. Construction starts in 2027, production in the early 2030s, capacity up to 200K vehicles a year.

European OEM results were mixed. Mercedes and VW cited rising China competition, VW and Stellantis cited pressure from Chinese OEMs in Europe, and Mercedes lowered its full-year EBIT outlook partly on higher material costs. Stellantis, Renault and VW also cited cost headwinds.
Symbotic and Walmart expanded their agreement to automate 25 US regional distribution centers, with an initial commitment of about $6 bn in spend over several years.

Autonomy news: Tesla FSD approved in Latvia, Aurora MoU with Charger Logistics for up to 500 trucks over 2027-2028, Agility Robotics expanded with GXO and announced early paid programs, Waymo named Toyota as an OEM partner starting in Japan in 2027, and Kodiak agreed to deploy 75 driverless trucks with DTL Transport.
China retail auto sales were down 26% yoy for October 1-25 and down 22% YTD per CNEVPost. NEV sales fell 13% yoy in the period and are down 13% YTD.

US Average Marketed Price was $52,400 as of 10/30, up about $3,000 from $49,431 on March 26, 2025 and slightly down from about $52,500 the prior week. US active new vehicle inventory was about 3.01 mn units, down about 56K yoy and flat week on week.
earnings_insights: VRT reported CY3Q revenue 15% above consensus and profit (EPS) 21% above, with 4Q/FY revenue guide 5% above and EPS guide 6% above consensus (FactSet). Stock +16% T+1.
APH reported CY3Q revenue 8% above consensus and EPS 10% above, with 4Q revenue guide 6% above and EPS guide 9% above consensus. Stock +4% T+1.

FLEX reported CY3Q revenue 4% above consensus and EPS 11% above, with FY revenue guide 2% above and EPS guide 7% above consensus (consensus may not reflect the closed EPC acquisition). Stock +12% T+1.
GM reported CY3Q revenue 3% above consensus and EBIT in line, with FY EBIT guide 2% below consensus. Stock -7% T+1.
Ford reported CY3Q revenue 1% above consensus and EBIT 12% above, with FY EBIT guide 1% above consensus. Stock +3% T+1.
Mobileye reported CY3Q revenue 3% above consensus and EBIT 14% above, with FY revenue and EBIT guides in line with consensus. Stock -9% T+1.
Tesla reported CY3Q revenue 1% below consensus and EPS 7% above. Stock -3% T+1.
TE Connectivity reported CY3Q revenue in line and EPS 2% above consensus, with 4Q revenue guide 4% above and EPS guide 10% above. Stock -2% T+1.
Gentex reported CY3Q revenue 3% below consensus and EBIT 6% below, with FY revenue guide 1% below and EBIT guide 3% below. Stock -5% T+1.
Visteon reported CY3Q revenue 4% above consensus and EBITDA 1% above, with FY EBITDA guide 1% below (excluding the warranty-related headwind). Stock -4% T+1.
BorgWarner reported CY3Q revenue in line and EPS 11% above consensus, with FY revenue guide 1% below and EPS guide 1% above. Stock -5% T+1.
Magna reported CY3Q revenue 1% below consensus and EPS 15% above, with FY revenue and EPS guides 1% below. Stock -1% T+1.
Lear reported CY3Q revenue 1% below consensus and EBIT in line, with FY revenue guide 1% below and EBIT guide in line. Stock +1% T+1.
Sensata reported CY3Q revenue and EPS 1% above consensus (excluding the one-time EV termination benefit), with 4Q revenue guide 2% below and EPS guide in line. Stock -3% T+1.
Rivian reported CY3Q revenue 8% above consensus. Stock +6% T+1.
Belden reported CY3Q revenue and EPS in line with consensus, with 4Q revenue guide 1% above and EPS guide in line. Stock +1% T+1.

Upcoming: APTV reports 3Q26 EPS pre-open November 3, VGNT pre-open November 4, AEVA post-close November 4, and INVZ pre-open the week of November 13. FLEX hosts an investor day November 10 and MGA on November 11.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS industry discussions point to October auto sales tracking at a SAAR in the high 15 mn range, ahead of the November 3 sales release.
China auto demand is weak, which weighs on global auto unit volumes.
NEV sales are also declining year over year.
Up about $3,000 from the March 26, 2025 tariff announcement and slightly down week on week. Pricing fell yoy for full-size pickups and rose for other key segments.
Down about 56K yoy and flat week on week. Inventory is up yoy for full-size pickups and down in other key segments.

risk_factors: Commodity and logistics cost inflation is a roughly $2 bn yoy headwind for Ford in 2027 and a similar issue for GM.
Muted global auto unit volumes, with weakness in China and a challenging European market.
Tariff uncertainty on Canadian steel and autos.
Datacenter revenue at hyperscalers was mixed versus expectations in the quarter.
geopolitical: US and Canada are reportedly working on a deal to ease Section 232 tariffs on Canadian steel and autos.
A 8/24 post from President Trump said US tariffs on Canadian autos and parts could rise to 50% from 25% starting January 2027.
Several European OEMs cited rising Chinese competition in China and pressure from Chinese OEMs in Europe.
